name: Leg Press
machineIdentification: A reclined seat facing a large angled foot platform loaded with plates or a stack. Look for the safety handles beside the seat that lock and unlock the sled.
instructions: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad.
Place your feet shoulder width on the middle of the platform.
Press the sled up and release the safety handles.
Lower until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Press back up without locking your knees.
keyCues: Keep your lower back flat against the seat.
Push through your whole foot, not just the toes.
Stop before your hips curl off the pad.
commonMistakes: Going so deep the lower back rounds off the pad.
Slamming the knees into full lockout.
Letting the knees cave inward under load.

name: Hack Squat Machine
machineIdentification: An angled sled you stand inside, with shoulder pads above and a foot platform below. You face away from the machine, back against the pad.
instructions: Step in with your shoulders under the pads and back flat.
Set your feet shoulder width in the middle of the platform.
Straighten your legs and release the safety handles.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel.
Drive back up without locking out hard.
keyCues: Keep your whole back pressed into the pad.
Track your knees out over your toes.
Control the descent — take two seconds.
commonMistakes: Letting the heels lift off the platform.
Bouncing out of the bottom position.
Placing the feet too low, which strains the knees.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest, cupping the top end.
Stand with feet slightly wider than your shoulders.
Squat down between your knees, keeping your chest tall.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive back up through your heels.
keyCues: Keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom.
Keep the dumbbell tight to your chest.
Push your knees out as you descend.
commonMistakes: Letting the chest collapse forward.
Rising onto the toes at the bottom.
Cutting the depth short by a long way.

name: Barbell Back Squat
machineIdentification: A power rack with the barbell set at upper-chest height and safety bars either side, set at roughly hip height.
instructions: Set the bar just below shoulder height and the safeties at hip height.
Step under and rest the bar across your upper back, not your neck.
Unrack and take two steps back, feet shoulder width.
Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive back up, keeping your chest lifted.
keyCues: Brace your core as if bracing for a punch.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.
Keep the bar over the middle of your feet.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips shoot up first out of the bottom.
Knees collapsing inward under heavier loads.
Skipping the safety bars entirely.

name: Smith Machine Squat
machineIdentification: A barbell locked inside vertical rails. Twist the bar to lock or release it at any height — useful because you can bail safely.
instructions: Set the bar at upper-back height and load it.
Step under so the bar rests across your upper back.
Walk your feet slightly forward of the bar.
Unlock and squat until your thighs are parallel.
Drive up and re-lock the bar at the top of the last rep.
keyCues: Set your feet a little forward — the rails fix the bar path.
Keep your weight in your mid-foot and heels.
Re-lock the bar before stepping out.
commonMistakes: Standing with feet directly under the bar, which strains the knees.
Locking the knees hard at the top of each rep.
Forgetting the bar is locked and trying to squat anyway.

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder width, toes turned out slightly.
Reach your arms forward for balance.
Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel.
Stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
keyCues: Sit back and down, not straight down.
Keep your heels flat on the floor.
Take three seconds to descend to make it harder.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Letting the knees cave in.
Rushing reps and losing depth as you tire.

name: Leg Extension Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with a padded roller that sits across the front of your ankles, and a weight stack behind. You straighten your legs against the roller.
instructions: Set the back pad so your knees line up with the machine's pivot.
Set the ankle roller to rest just above your feet.
Sit back and hook your shins behind the roller.
Straighten your legs fully.
Lower under control without letting the stack touch down.
keyCues: Pause for a beat at the top with quads squeezed.
Keep your hips planted in the seat.
Lower slowly — three seconds.
commonMistakes: Swinging the weight up with a hip thrust.
Letting the stack slam at the bottom of each rep.
Setting the pivot wrong so the knees take the strain.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
machineIdentification: Any flat bench plus dumbbells. Your rear foot rests on the bench behind you.
instructions: Stand about two feet in front of a bench, dumbbells at your sides.
Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is parallel.
Drive up through your front heel.
Finish all reps, then switch legs.
keyCues: Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Move straight up and down, not forward and back.
Lean the torso slightly forward to bias the glutes.
commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench, cramping the front knee.
Pushing off the rear foot to help.
Losing balance and cutting the range short.

name: Walking Lunge
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides.
Step forward into a lunge until both knees are at 90 degrees.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
Step through directly into the next lunge with the other leg.
keyCues: Take a long enough step that the front shin stays vertical.
Keep your torso upright.
Lower the back knee to just above the floor.
commonMistakes: Short steps that push the front knee way past the toes.
Letting the rear knee bang into the floor.
Leaning forward over the front leg.

name: Dumbbell Step-up
machineIdentification: A flat bench or a plyo box roughly knee height, plus dumbbells.
instructions: Stand facing a knee-height bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Place one whole foot on the bench.
Drive through that heel to stand up on the bench.
Step back down under control.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
keyCues: Push through the top foot, don't hop off the bottom one.
Keep the working foot flat on the bench.
Lower slowly instead of dropping down.
commonMistakes: Pushing off the trailing leg to get up.
Using a box so high the hip has to hike.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
